artifacts.summary: 7-phase, 5.5-hour implementation plan covering all 6 work items and all 5 acceptance criteria for activating and hardening the Zotero write-back path.

summary: Created a 7-phase plan (5.5 hours, 6 dependency waves) for the Zotero write-back activation. Phase 1 re-confirms the environment (zot v0.10.0 confirmed live at plan time) and captures the zot schema surface. Phase 2 corrects stale docs across five files. Phase 3 wires zotero-export-freshness.sh into both write branches of literature-ingest-online.sh. Phase 4 adds DOI normalization plus a hard-stop live-library dedup via zotero-read.sh search. Phase 5 records evidence that the %PDF gate, DOI-only-fallback honest surfacing, never-fabricate-keys stop, and the zotero-write.sh choke-point are unchanged. Phase 6 performs the live envelope confirmation behind a hard user-confirmation gate against the production library. Phase 7 activates the literature extension for the first time via a headless manager.load call, resyncs, and verifies byte identity.

memory_candidates.content: A documented 'deployment status' table inside an extension's own README can drift arbitrarily far from the live deploy tree when the extension has no entry in the project's extension-state file (.claude-extensions.json). The non-destructive deploy resync only force-resyncs extensions the state file already marks active, so running it repeatedly on an unregistered extension silently deploys nothing -- the operation succeeds and changes nothing. Any plan whose step is 'deploy these scripts through the normal deploy flow' must first verify the owning extension is registered as active; if it is not, first-time activation (a manager.load call or one pass through the interactive picker) is a prerequisite, not an implementation detail. The correct diagnostic is to read the extension-state file's keys, never the extension's own documentation. Activation is an operation, not a source edit, so it can satisfy a source-store/deploy boundary rule that forbids editing the deploy tree or another extension's source.
